newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian bank system is drag on growth - Amato.
newsitem.headline: Italian bank system is drag on growth - Amato.

text.p: Italian banks are overstaffed, unprofitable, weighed down by bad debt and unable to sustain a competitive economy, President of Italy's anti-trust authority Giuliano Amato said on Thursday.

"The Italian banking world is not in a position to sustain the competitiveness of the Italian economic system in the international theatre," Amato told news magasine Panorama in an interview released ahead of publication.
Amato, a former prime minister, said none of Italy's banks were nearly as large as any of the top European or U.S. banks.

"Italian banks have a rather modest level of profitability, between 0.5 and two percent, with a very high level of problem loans which in the view of some people, comes close to the value of their equity," said Amato.
He said most banks were run by bureaucrats used to carrying out orders of the Bank of Italy or the Treasury to the letter, a legacy of strict banking laws dating back to the 1930s.
"After the great depression and the banking law of 1936, salvation was sought by putting faith in the state rather than in the market," he added.

Amato said getting Italian banks to adopt a market-oriented culture was similar to the challenge faced by former state industries in Eastern Europe, "with one difference, the successes in the East are greater than those shown by our banks."

Amato said one of the reasons that a 1990 law bearing his name had failed to trigger a spate of mergers in the banking industry was that many banks had strong local traditions dating back to the middle ages. -- Milan newsroom +392-66102321
